headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/network on transformers create dangerous default interaction risks with cognee's data-rich memory workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests documents, workflows, and support history, while transformers can run browsers and process files; if cognee outputs are fed into transformers as prompts or instructions, file/content injection is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are copied into transformers prompts without sanitization
IF transformers reads cognee-generated files as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a strict prompt/content delimiter before passing outputs
Strip executable-looking directives from shared text
Use a read-only handoff file with a fixed schema
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history; transformers can read and write files and has broad network egress. If both share a workspace, sensitive material can move from cognee into transformers and then out through model or hub calls. This is a default-risk pathway, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace directory
IF transformers processes files containing personal or finance data
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove sensitive files before transformer runs
Disable network egress for transformer jobs handling sensitive data
Check file permissions on the shared directory
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and transformers can write the filesystem, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses. If they operate on the same directory or mutable artifacts, concurrent writes and state corruption are likely. Because the profiles show overlapping write-capable surfaces and no locking, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF either agent mutates shared model or cache files without locks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Make shared artifacts read-only
Verify lock files exist before execution
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while transformers can run pipelines that may consume those outputs. If transformers treats cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream processing. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show direct autonomous action-taking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF transformers consumes cognee output without validation
IF downstream pipeline actions are triggered from parsed cognee results
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Require schema validation on cognee outputs
Compare outputs against a second source
Log and diff transformed fields before use
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while transformers has broad file and network capabilities but no residency or compliance controls documented. If regulated data reaches transformers, compliance breach risk is material and defaults are unsafe. Uncertainty about controls escalates severity.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data is processed by transformers
IF no data-processing agreement or residency control is configured
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from transformer inputs
Route regulated workloads to a compliant environment
Confirm retention settings for both agents
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention enforcement
